Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards. Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

Coker caught four of five targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. It was yet another quiet game from Coker, who has been held below 40 receiving yards in four of the last five games. Since his massive 8-138-2 receiving line in Week 1, Coker has averaged just 3.8 catches for 65.5 receiving yards per game over his last six contests. He has only one touchdown during that span. Coker will be in a bounce-back spot against the Saints at the Superdome next Sunday.

Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts. Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the season thus far, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine contests.

Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Shrader entered Week 9 having made just three field goals over the team's last three games, but he got back on track Sunday. The kicker made a 47-yard attempt in the third quarter before adding makes from 59 and 50 yards in the final quarter. Shrader has now converted multiple field-goal attempts in six contests this year, and he's gone 22-for-24 on field-goal tries, including 8-for-9 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

Johnson played all 17 of his snaps on special teams and recorded one tackle in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Johnson, a reserve wide receiver, has been used almost exclusively on special teams through his two-plus seasons in Tampa Bay. He's logged just 15 total snaps on offense through nine games in 2026, recording a three-yard reception on two targets. Johnson leads the Buccaneers with 14 kickoff returns for 389 yards, but he didn't see any runback opportunities in Week 9 while Sean Tucker handled those duties.

Commanders head coach Dan Quinn ruled out Yankoff (knee) for Thursday night's games against the Giants, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports. Yankoff did not participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice after missing Monday with a knee injury. Week 10 will be Washington's first game without the 26-year-old, though the injury is not presumed to be serious. Yankoff has three catches on five targets, for 22 yards through eight games.

Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries. The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

Wilson totaled six tackles (three solo) and an interception during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday. Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

Whittington (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday. This is another blow to the Rams' receiving corps, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR and Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is slated to miss several weeks. Whittington would have had a chance to carve out a major role in Los Angeles' wideout room, but instead he'll be sidelined until at least Dec. 20. The Rams signed Xavier Smith off San Francisco's practice squad Tuesday to take Whittington's place on the 53-man roster and in the WR corps.

Johnson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday against the Falcons in Madrid. Johnson suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus the Titans, and he subsequently followed a DNP/LP/FP practice regimen during Week 9 prep before getting a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's international matchup. Now that he's confirmed to be active, he should be good for his normal 20-30 percent weekly defensive snap share.
questionable questionable

Isaac (hamstring) is questionable to return to Thursday night's contest against the Jaguars. Isaac is nursing a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. The linebacker operates primarily as a special-teams option, so his absence doesn't have any impact on Baltimore's defensive approach.

Walker didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars. Walker made little impact in Thursday night's loss, playing 15 offensive snaps behind Ja'Kobi Lane (32), Rashod Bateman (35) and Zay Flowers (37). Walker will likely see a similar role as the season progresses.

Barner caught two of four targets for seven yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. He added three carries for three yards and an additional touchdown. Barner was the Seahawks' closer, finishing off both touchdown drives with short scores against Arizona. His first was a one-yard rushing touchdown, and Barner then caught a seven-yard score from Drew Lock. Both touchdowns came in the second quarter. For the season, Barner has 23 grabs for 210 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets. He's also rushed for two scores. Barner is in the large group of touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at tight end.

Allen rushed eight times for 33 yards, caught both of his targets for 21 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Allen was limited to 10 touches in Breece Hall's (quadriceps) return from a five-game absence, while Hall turned 18 touches into 87 yards. The 22-year-old Allen excelled during Hall's absence, topping 100 scrimmage yards in each of the previous four games, but Allen will be tough to trust moving forward in fantasy with Hall first in line for touches, especially in the negative game scripts that will likely persist for the 2-7 Jets. Allen's lost fumble was his first of the season, and he has put the ball on the ground only one other time, so at least ball security hasn't been an issue for him heading into a Week 10 home game against the Bills.

Davis didn't play any offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. With Breece Hall back from his quad injury to form a backfield duo with Braelon Allen, Davis was relegated to RB3 duties and played 16 snaps on special teams. Davis has rushed 15 times for 44 yards, while recording five grabs for 68 yards on six targets across nine appearances this season.
questionable questionable

Lloyd (knee) is not listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday. The running back appears ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Vikings after missing Week 9 against New England. With Josh Jacobs (finger) set to miss some time, Lloyd figures to be part of the backfield mix, joining Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong.

Hopper (chest) was a limited participant in Wednesday's jog-through practice. Hopper picked up a chest injury during the first quarter of the Packers' win against the Patriots in Week 9 and did not return. The good news for the third-year pro is that he was cleared to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday. If Hopper can upgrade his participation over the next two days, then he would likely avoid an injury designation for Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Vikings.

Bengals head coach Zac Taylor confirmed Wednesday that All has been diagnosed with a torn ACL in his right knee and will require season-ending surgery, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports. All, who sustained the injury in Sunday's win over the Ravens, has now torn the ACL in his right knee three times during his career. He first tore the ACL during his final collegiate season at Iowa in 2023, then had his 2024 rookie campaign with the Bengals cut short after damaging the ligament again. Given the timing of the injury along with the fact that he'll be working his way back from a third surgery of the same knee, All is far from guaranteed to be ready to play when the 2027 season gets underway.

Knight (hip) doesn't have an injury designation for Monday's game against the Bears, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Knight opened Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices before logging a full session Saturday, and he's done enough to fade an injury tag against Chicago. The third-year linebacker has seen an uptick in defensive snaps over his last two outings, and he's logged 16 tackles (nine solo) in that span.

Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Gould is in line to step into the slot role previously held by Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. With both Downs and Keenan Allen having been dealt by the Colts on Tuesday, the team will be operating with a re-shaped WR corps going forward. According to the Colts' latest unofficial depth chart, Gould is indeed listed a first-teamer along with Ashton Dulin and Laquon Treadwell. Also expected to have additional opportunities in the coming weeks will be 2026 seventh-rounder Deion Burks, with veteran pass catcher Nick Westbrook-Ikhine in the mix as well after being signed off the practice squad. Though a wait-and-see approach is in order in term's of Gould's fantasy lineup viability, his production beginning this weekend versus Miami is worth tracking by those in deeper PPR formats.

Eboigbe is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Houston due to an ankle injury, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports. Eboigbe was hurt in the first quarter, and his return is uncertain. Nick Barrett will likely pick up more defensive snaps for as long as Eboigbe remains sidelined.

Smith (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears. Smith was limited at practice by an ankle issue Wednesday and Thursday, but he managed to practice in full Friday and will avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend. He projects to start at safety next to Antoine Winfield in Week 9.

Johnson wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The tight end played just 12 offensive snaps, logging a 17.9 percent snap share against Philly. On the season, Johnson has just four catches for 55 yards and a touchdown on nine targets across six appearances. He has no fantasy appeal with Isaiah Likely healthy.

Harrison (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports. It's a new injury for the Texans' newest wideout, who has produced just six catches for 60 yards and a touchdown on 11 targets through three games with Houston. Harrison ran just 14 routes on 40 dropbacks last Sunday against the Chargers, tying him with Kayshon Boutte for fourth among Texans wideouts. Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell appear to have emerged as the Nos. 2 and 3 receivers behind Nico Collins.

Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions while adding one rush for three yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.

Head coach Todd Bowles suggested Monday that McMillan (knee) isn't likely to immediately return to action following the Buccaneers' Week 10 bye, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports. While Bowles indicated that linebacker Yaya Diaby (knee) has decent odds of playing in the Buccaneers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Lions, the coach was less optimistic about McMillan's chances of being ready to play in Week 11. The Buccaneers have yet to open McMillan's 21-day practice window, after he was placed on injured reserve Sept. 30 due to a PCL sprain in his left knee, which was an aggravation of a previous injury. Bowles noted that McMillan underwent a medical procedure on the knee shortly after landing on IR and is still dealing with some discomfort.

Rakestraw (ankle) does not have a game designation for Sunday's Week 8 tilt versus the Vikings. Rakestraw suffered an ankle injury late in this past Sunday's win over Green Bay. He was held to limited practice sessions Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday. As such, Rakestraw is good to go for Sunday's big battle against Minnesota.

Bullard (ankle) was held out of Wednesday's jog-through practice. Bullard may have tweaked his ankle during the Packers' win over the Patriots in Week 9, when he logged three tackles (two solo). He'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, but if he cannot play in that contest, then Kamal Hadden, Carrington Valentine and Benjamin St-Juste would all be in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary.

Franklin brought in three of four targets for 31 yards during the Broncos' 26-21 win over the Panthers on Sunday. Franklin drew a 27-yard pass interference penalty on the Broncos' second offensive play of the game, but the third-year wide receiver didn't log his first catch until early in the fourth quarter. He has operated in a rotational role for most of the season, and even with Jaylen Waddle in the league's concussion protocol, Franklin will likely maintain that workload following the Broncos' Week 10 bye.

Wright (quadriceps) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports. After missing last Sunday's loss to the Lions, Wright figures to be back in as the lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon, though Wright has not produced when on the field this season. He's averaged 1,9 yards per carry on 22 attempts and is virtually a zero in the passing game.

Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings. Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

Washington caught two of three targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 19-9 loss to the Lions. Washington was held in check by Detroit's suspect secondary, failing to reel in at least three passes for the first time this season. In addition, his 21 receiving yards were also a season low. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 70 receiving yards in a game this year, and he has reached the end zone only once. Washington will have an opportunity to get back on track against the sputtering Colts in Week 10.

Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.

Worthy (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice for Kansas City. Worthy was considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets in the fourth quarter. A quick return to full practice participation suggests Worthy will be fine for the upcoming matchup with Atlanta on Sunday, but his target share may decline in the second half of the season after Kansas City traded for WR Josh Downs.

Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets. Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

Newton (pectoral) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams. The 24-year-old was reinstated from injured reserve Saturday but was still officially questionable to play Sunday versus Los Angeles. Newton is ready to make his season debut after recovering from surgery to repair a torn pectoral muscle in August.

Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. He also gained 16 rushing yards on four carries and lost a fumble. The lost fumble was the first giveaway of the season for Daniels in six games. The third-year QB also struggled to sustain drives while working with a badly depleted wide receiver room, and his lone TD was a seven-yard toss to Van Jefferson -- a player who had zero catches on the year coming into Sunday -- in the second quarter. Injuries have derailed the first half of the season for the Commanders, but Daniels will try to spark his team to life in Week 10 against the Giants.

Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries. It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

Williams completed 22 of 37 passes for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. He also rushed five times for 16 yards. Williams looked unstoppable early, capping Chicago's two first-quarter drives with touchdown passes of nine yards to Rome Odunze and 56 yards to Luther Burden, the latter of whom later exited due to a concussion. The 2024 first overall pick cooled down after that, throwing three second-quarter interceptions en route to a career-worst four interceptions overall. Chicago's defense picked up the slack with a pick-six against Baker Mayfield, and Williams found Colston Loveland for a 38-yard gain to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning field goal on the game's final play. The Bears have reeled off four consecutive wins since Williams returned from a hamstring injury to improve to 7-2, and he didn't have a turnover in the previous three games prior to Sunday night's downturn. Williams will look to clean up the errors in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Odunze caught four of seven targets for 60 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Odunze bobbled what should have been an easy touchdown catch and failed to get down inbounds by the time he secured the ball, but he made amends two plays later with his first touchdown catch of the season to cap Chicago's opening drive from nine yards out. He had another critical drop later in the game but still finished second on the team behind Luther Burden (concussion) in targets, catches and receiving yards. Burden exited late in the game, and if Chicago's Week 10 bye doesn't provide the team's leading receiver enough time to clear concussion protocol, Odunze could get an uptick in opportunities in Week 11 against the Saints.

McCarthy (hip) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. McCarthy was sidelined for most of the third quarter of this past Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles after sustaining a painful hip pointer, but he was able to finish out the game. Head coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence afterward that the injury wouldn't be anything that jeopardized McCarthy's status for Thursday's game against the Commanders, and the quarterback's ability to take every rep Tuesday clears the way for him to start on a short week. Through two starts and two appearances off the bench with the Giants, McCarthy has completed 43 of 68 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 622 yards (9.1 YPA), one touchdown and one interception to go with 51 yards on nine carries.

Williams (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice. It's a new injury for Williams, who previously missed a chunk of the season with an ankle injury. He's been running as the Packers' clear third receiver behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson over the last few weeks. If Williams is unable to play against Minnesota on Sunday, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant could see an uptick in snaps, though Skyy Moore (ankle) had his 21-day practice window opened and could also be an option.

McCord will step in as the Dolphins' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game at Indianapolis after Miami placed Malik Willis (core) on injured reserve Tuesday, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports. A 2025 sixth-round pick of the Eagles, McCord will be making his NFL debut Sunday, after he had been active for each of the 1-7 Dolphins' first eight games but didn't see any playing time behind Willis. Before landing with the Dolphins in a trade prior to Week 1, the 24-year-old signal-caller looked sharp during preseason action as a member of the Packers, completing 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT while adding 16 yards on five carries over three games. Expectations should still be held in check for McCord in his first regular-season action, especially while he'll be working with one of the NFL's weaker collections of skill-position players. The Dolphins are optimistic that Willis will be able to return from IR before the end of the season, but McCord should be primed for at least a four-game run as the team's starter while Willis is sidelined.

Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

Waxter (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Texans. The special-teamer will not return to Sunday's contest after exiting in the first quarter. A number of players could step up to contribute on special teams in Waxter's absence.

Jeanty rushed six times for 25 yards while catching five of seven targets for minus-5 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The Raiders largely abandoned the run after going down 14-0 early, but Jeanty was more effective with his six carries than Mike Washington, who rushed six times for minus-3 yards and finished without a target. Sunday's even distribution in carries was a positive development for Jeanty, who had just two rushing attempts to Washington's 25 in the Week 8 win over the Jets. Jeanty still has more receiving yards (371) than rushing yards (362) and is averaging just 3.2 yards per carry heading into a difficult Week 10 matchup against Seattle's elite front seven.

McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

Loveland caught four of six targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers. Loveland was quiet for most of the night but got free for a 38-yard catch in the final minute to set up Cairo Santos' game-winning 38-yard field goal on the game's final play. The 2025 first-round pick has recorded at least 54 receiving yards in five of the past six games, having bounced back from a slow start to his sophomore season during which Loveland compiled just 34 yards through three games. Loveland will try to keep building momentum in Week 11 against the Saints following Chicago's Week 10 bye.

Warren may see more targets after the Colts traded wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday, Chris Bumbaca of ColtsWire reports. The trade deadline went as well as possible for Warren's fantasy value, considering the Colts moved their top wide receivers but avoided an all-out purge. The only problem is that Warren is already averaging 7.6 targets per game (fourth among TEs) and producing just 39.3 receiving yards per game and 7.2 yards per catch. Efficiency has been the issue, not volume, and the Colts will likely lean on their running game after declining to trade RB Jonathan Taylor. Improved play from Warren and QB Daniel Jones would probably matter more than another increase in target share.

Egbuka (foot) caught three of five targets for 38 yards and added a one-yard run in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Egbuka returned from a two-game absence during which he was in concussion protocol in addition to dealing with a foot injury. He tied for second on the team in targets behind Cade Otton's eight and finished third in receiving yards behind Tez Johnson (76) and Kenny Gainwell (60), as Baker Mayfield spread the ball around to complement Bucky Irving's two-touchdown effort on the ground. Egbuka hasn't exceeded 63 yards in seven appearances this season heading into Tampa Bay's Week 10 bye.

Williams failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina. Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

Walley (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. After being injured in Week 7, Walley has missed the past two games but appears ready to return to the lineup Sunday against the Dolphins. He's spent most of his time covering the slot for the Colts this season, recording 35 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and three pass breakups across seven appearances.

Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports. After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.

Parrish registered seven total tackles (four solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 16-0 win over Atlanta. Parrish was able to notch multiple passes defensed for the fifth straight game, and he was able to reel in his second interception of the year, jumping in front of a short pass from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix in the second quarter. The cornerback has now compiled 36 total tackles (30 solo) and 13 passes defensed, including two interceptions, over seven contests so far during the 2026 regular season.

Felton went without a target while playing six of the Vikings' 48 offensive snaps in Monday's 23-6 loss to the Bills. Felton continues to handle a muted role as a depth receiver for Minnesota, as Monday marked the third consecutive game in which he played single-digit snaps. For the season, the second-year wideout out of Maryland has been limited to just three receptions for 41 yards on seven targets over eight appearances.

Carter recorded nine tackles (three solo) and a pass defense during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens. Carter didn't play every defensive snap for just the first time this season, but his nine stops were tied with Bryan Cook for most on the Bengals. Carter has logged at least five stops in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 50 tackles (22 solo), including 1.5 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble in 2026.

Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards while catching three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss against the Saints. Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.

Ayomanor caught three of five targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. Even with Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Ayomanor's role didn't grow much, as Wan'Dale Robinson, Gunnar Helm and Chimere Dike combined to see 22 of the team's 39 targets. Through eight games this season, Ayomanor has 13 grabs for 211 yards and a touchdown on 26 targets.

Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.

Ingram-Dawkins exited Monday night's game against the Bills with an ankle injury and is questionable to return. Levi Drake Rodriguez, Elijah Williams and Jalen Redmond will handle more of the defensive-line duties with Ingram-Dawkins sidelined.

James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas. As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

Giddens was active but didn't play in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.

Lambert-Smith registered one catch (on four targets) for 50 yards in Sunday's loss to Houston. Lambert-Smith wasn't exactly prolific in spite of logging a hearty 40 offensive snaps, but he made his one catch count, hauling in a 50-yard reception in the third quarter. However, the woeful Chargers turned the ball over on a fumble two plays later. Lambert-Smith has spent much of the season on IR and has had an inconsistent role when suiting up, but he was deployed pretty heavily Sunday because Ladd McConkey couldn't play due to back spasms. If McConkey is also sidelined next Monday in Baltimore, Lambert-Smith could again be a fairly big part of Los Angeles' air attack.

Evans caught both of his two targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 26-21 loss versus the Broncos. For the third game in a row, Evans drew exactly two targets and caught both of them Sunday. With that said, he also again trailed in snaps at tight end (31) behind teammates Tommy Tremble (46) and Darren Waller (35), both of whom also drew more targets in Week 9. Evans' role in the Panthers' passing offense isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats going into a Week 10 matchup at New Orleans.

Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday. Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

Hawes caught his lone target for eight yards during Buffalo's win over the Vikings on Monday. Hawes played a season-high 46 snaps on offense and also played eight snaps on special teams. The 25-year-old has now caught a pass in consecutive games after failing to record any receptions across his first six outings of the campaign.

Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

Borregales made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. Borregales didn't attempt a field goal, and it was the second time this season that he didn't kick any. For the year, the second-year kicker in 10 of 13 on FGAs and has made 23 of 24 extra points. He'll be a fantasy target for next Sunday's potential shootout in Detroit.

Harris (ankle) practiced in full Wednesday. The second-year cornerback was injured in the Week 8 overtime loss to the Bengals, but the bye came at the right time, and he appears to be ready to go for Sunday's date with the Jaguars. Harris has functioned as Tennessee's slot corner this season, so he figures to see plenty of Parker Washington in Week 10.

Lane recorded four total tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including a pick-six, during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. Lane played every one of the team's defensive snaps in Week 8, stepping into a starting role in the secondary with Antonio Johnson (ankle) unavailable. The 23-year-old's biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter when he jumped in front of a pass from Colts quarterback Daniel Jones for an interception, returning it 92 yards for his first career defensive touchdown. Lane has now compiled 20 total tackles (10 solo) and four passes defensed, including Sunday's pick-six, over seven contests during the 2026 campaign.
out out

Johnson caught two passes for 76 yards on five targets in Sunday night's 27-24 loss to the Bears. Johnson accounted for the Bucs' longest play of the game, producing a 58-yard catch-and-run to lead the team in receiving yards. Johnson has been working as the Bucs' WR3 behind Emeka Egbuka and Chris Godwin, with rookie Ted Hurst mixing in for sub-package snaps. Johnson isn't a particularly exciting fantasy bet.

Fitzgerald missed his only field-goal attempt and went 3-for-3 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos. Fitzgerald went without a field-goal make for the second time in three weeks, and he pushed his only field-goal attempt of the day wide right from 43 yards in the second quarter. The miss was his first on a field-goal try this year, and the kicker now has gone 13-for-14 on field-goal attempts, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, while making 16 of 21 extra-point attempts over eight regular-season contests so far.

Latu caught his lone target for a 25-yard touchdown Monday in a 23-6 win against the Vikings. Latu gave the Bills the lead late in the first half when he got open in the back of the end zone and caught a pass from Josh Allen. It was not only his first catch of the campaign but also his first NFL touchdown. Latu has worked primarily on special teams this season, and despite his score Monday, he isn't likely to suddenly be a big part of the passing game given the fact that Dalton Kincaid, Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes all remain ahead of him on the tight-end depth chart.

Collins (hip) is listed as active Sunday against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports. On cutdown day Aug. 30, the Falcons placed Collins on IR with a designation to return, which would have allowed him to practice as early as Week 3 prep. Instead, his hip injury kept him out of drills until Week 7, when his 21-day window opened, but he sat out the last two games before Atlanta finally activated him Saturday. With Zachariah Branch sidelined Sunday due to a hamstring issue, Collins will serve as a reserve WR along with Chris Blair behind Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus.

Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

Brosmer completed six of seven attempts for 58 yards in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills. Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

Price caught one of his four targets for six yards in a Week 9 loss to Buffalo on Monday Night Football. He also gained 12 yards on one punt return and brought back four kickoffs for 124 yards. Price wasn't the only Minnesota pass catcher who logged an inefficient line, as starting quarterback Carson Wentz completed just eight of 25 pass attempts. Price did make an impact in the return game by averaging 31.0 yards on his four kickoff returns. Price's role continues to be mostly centered on special teams, as he's caught just four passes for 32 yards on 11 targets through eight games.

Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

Chism caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers. Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.

Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams. Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

Marks (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports. In this past Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, Marks played on 66 percent of the Texans' snaps on offense, while carrying 18 carries times for 70 yards and catching one of his four targets for four yards. He's been working as the team's clear-cut RB1 in the absence of David Montgomery (groin), who didn't practice Wednesday, with further context regarding the the backfield duo's Week 10 status on track to arrive no later than Thursday's practice report.

Helm caught five of nine targets for 76 yards during Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. Helm led the team in targets while he was able to register a new career-high 76 receiving yards in the contest. The tight end has now reeled in eight passes over the last two weeks after he caught nine of 13 targets for 60 yards over the first six games of the 2026 campaign. Helm will have a tough test against the Jaguars in Week 10 after the team's bye week in Week 9.

Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

Porter (groin) is active for Sunday's Week 9 battle against the 49ers. Porter suffered a groin injury last Sunday against the Jets and logged a DNP/LP/FP practice progression this week. He was questionable to suit up entering Sunday but will ultimately be able to give it a go. Porter ranks second on the Raiders with five defensed passes on the season.

Etienne carried the ball two times for seven yards and returned one punt for nine yards during Carolina'a loss Sunday to the Broncos. Etienne once again saw limited action offensively, playing just seven snaps. The 2025 fourth-round pick was the only running back other than Chuba Hubbard to record a carry and should continue to serve as the team's No. 2 back while Jonathon Brooks remains sidelined due to an abdomen injury.

Royals caught both of his targets for 18 yards Sunday in a 35-12 rout of the Jets. Royals ranked fourth among KC wideouts in offensive snaps (21), trailing Xavier Worthy (49), Rashee Rice (38) and Andrew Armstrong (22). Royals matched his season high with two catches, and the 18 receiving yards were his second-most in a game this season. That speaks to the minimal production he's provided thus far, and Royals' role could be further reduced with the Chiefs' acquisition of Josh Downs on Tuesday.

Horton caught two passes for 22 yards on three targets in Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals. Horton has just seven catches for 67 yards across six games since Week 3. The Seahawks' No. 3 receiver is well off the fantasy radar, even with Rashid Shaheed (knee) injured.

Fannin (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports. Fannin dealt with the groin issue in practice last week but ultimately avoided an injury designation ahead of last Sunday's overtime loss to the Saints. In that contest, Fannin caught both of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He had been silent for much of the game before producing a 39-yard touchdown in the extra frame. The overall TE7 in half-PPR points per game this season, Fannin has 37 catches for 453 yards and four touchdowns on 53 targets through nine appearances.

Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

Golden brought in all 10 targets for 164 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. Golden led the Packers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and the latter total was also a new career high. The second-year wideout also laid claim to the game's longest catch (49 yards), and he reeled in the first of Jordan Love's three TD passes on the day with a five-yard grab at just under the eight-minute mark of the first quarter. Golden now has four 100-yard efforts in what is already a breakout campaign that's seen him amass a 53-783-5 line on 92 targets heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday.

Sanders will return to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Texans after the Browns announced Wednesday that Deshaun Watson (concussion) will draw the Week 10 start, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports. Watson led the Browns to a 5-3 record over their first eight games before developing concussion symptoms and being placed in the NFL's five-step protocol last week. Though Watson cleared protocol last Saturday, his lack of on-field reps during the week prompted the Browns to keep him inactive for Sunday's matchup with the Saints. Sanders stepped in under center and overcame a slow start to finish with 297 passing yards, 28 rushing yards, two passing touchdowns and no turnovers in a 23-22 overtime loss, with his performance drawing praise from head coach Todd Monken. Though the Browns will go back to a healthy Watson for Week 10, Sanders' strong outing in New Orleans could put Watson on shakier ground atop the depth chart.

TeSlaa registered one catch for nine yards on two targets in Sunday's 19-9 win over Miami. Jared Goff threw to TeSlaa twice on Detroit's opening drive but didn't turn to him again for the remainder of the contest. The second-year wideout thus continued a very unproductive stretch, as he's logged just two catches for 19 yards on six targets over his past four games. TeSlaa is still working as Detroit's No. 3 wideout -- among Lions wide receivers, only Jameson Williams and Amon-Ra St. Brown logged more offensive snaps Sunday -- but looks just aren't coming his way. He'll try to break out of the funk next Sunday against New England.

Williams finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 10 tackles (four solo) and one interception. The second-year defensive back's 10 tackles were a career best, and his interception off Sam Darnold late in the second quarter was also the first of Williams' NFL career. Williams is up to 29 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and seven pass defenses (including one interception) through six regular-season games.

Milroe will get added reps at practice ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports. Milroe is expected to serve as the top backup behind Drew Lock at quarterback in Week 9 with Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sidelined. Milroe has yet to appear in a regular-season contest this season and likely won't do so Sunday unless Lock is forced out of the contest with an injury.

Ward completed 26 of 40 passes for 304 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. He added seven rushing attempts for 41 yards, lost a fumble, ran in a two-point conversion and threw a successful two-point conversion. Ward threw two go-ahead touchdown passes in the fourth quarter, connecting with Chimere Dike for an 11-yard score before finding Wan'Dale Robinson for a 15-yard TD. Those two touchdown passes came after a streak of five Tony Pollard rushing touchdowns without a Ward passing TD over the previous seven quarters. Pollard's second rushing touchdown Sunday was followed up by a two-point conversion from Ward on the ground, and Ward threw a two-point conversion to Gunnar Helm after the touchdown pass to Robinson to take a 36-29 lead. The Bengals answered with a game-tying touchdown, and Cincinnati scored to begin overtime. Tennessee's ensuing drive in OT resulted in a turnover on downs, but the bonus possession helped Ward reach 300 passing yards in a game for the first time in his career. Ward's first multi-touchdown passing performance of the season improves his TD:INT to 6:5 heading into a Week 10 home game against the Jaguars following Tennessee's Week 9 bye.

Carter (knee/back) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Commanders. Carter logged limited tags Monday and Tuesday before upgrading to full practice Wednesday. Across eight starts this season, the No. 3 overall pick of the 2025 Draft has produced 19 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble. He's yet to develop into a game-wrecking edge rusher.

The Steelers designated Harmon (foot) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports. Harmon said he's 100 percent healthy, but the team will take things day-to-day with the defensive lineman, according to Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com. Harmon hasn't played since Week 4. He's recorded 12 tackles (three solo), including 1.5 sacks, across 85 defensive snaps this season.

Starks finished Baltimore's Week 9 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday with four tackles (three solo) and a forced fumble. Starks tied for third on his team in tackles during a rather uninspiring performance on both offense and defense by the Ravens. He did make a big play when he forced a fumble that was recovered by Baltimore in the third quarter, but the Ravens turned the ball over on downs on four plays on their ensuing possession. Starks logged 84 tackles over 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, and he's well on his way to surpassing that mark with 55 stops (including 1.0 sacks) through nine contests in 2026.

Gabriel "will serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.

Dike caught five of six targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 43-36 overtime loss to the Bengals. With Carnell Tate (shoulder) inactive against Cincinnati, Dike receiving the biggest playing-time boost on offense, as he ran 40 routes on Cam Ward's 46 dropbacks. Only Gunnar Helm produced more receiving yards than Dike in the Week 8 defeat, and only Wan'Dale Robinson (six) recorded more catches. With the Titans headed into their Week 9 bye, Tate figures to be back the following week versus Jacksonville. Perhaps Dike can earn more playing time at Elic Ayomanor's expense, and Calvin Ridley's name has been linked to trade speculation.
out out

The 49ers plan to open West's (undisclosed) practice window Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports. West was placed on injured reserve in late September due to an undisclosed injury but is now nearing his return. Once the practice window is officially opened, San Francisco will have 21 days to activate the 2025 fourth-round pick, or else he'll be forced to stay on injured reserve for the remainder of the campaign.

Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Prior to Tuesday's practice, Skattebo told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the hamstring tear he sustained in a Week 7 overtime win over the Texans "wasn't too bad" and wouldn't prevent him from playing Thursday against the Commanders. With Skattebo proceeding to take every rep during Tuesday's session, he's now officially in the clear to step back into a lead role out of the New York backfield in Week 10. As a result of Skattebo's return to the lineup following a one-game absence, Devin Singletary -- who handled a season-high 23 touches in the Week 9 win over the Eagles -- is expected to see his opportunities get scaled back significantly.

Hunter caught his only target for minus-1 yard and lost a fumble in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens. Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.

Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in practice Wednesday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports. It remains to be seen if Tuten is simply managing a couple of aches and pains in the wake of Week 9 action or is in danger of missing the Jaguars' next game, so his status is worth tracking ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans. Fellow RB Chris Rodriguez also appeared on Wednesday's injury report after being deemed limited by a hand injury.

Ezeiruaku (ankle) is considered day-to-day, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports. Ezeiruaku suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Colts and didn't return. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the 49ers, Ezeiruaku may not be able to suit up for that one. If that's the case, Von Miller and Marist Liufau could see more snaps.

Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

Bech caught one of two targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to the 49ers. Bech logged a 34 percent offensive snap share, third-highest among Raiders wideouts behind Jalen Nailor (74 percent) and Tre Tucker (64 percent). Though he seems fairly secure in the No. 3 wideout role, Bech hasn't done much this season, producing no more than three catches or 25 yards in any of his five games to date.
out out

Burden has a concussion, head coach Ben Johnson revealed after Sunday's 27-24 win over the Buccaneers, Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com reports. Burden left the game in the fourth quarter after taking a high hit, and a subsequent evaluation has revealed a concussion for Chicago's leading receiver. He will have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol in order to be eligible to play in Week 11 against the Saints, with Chicago's Week 10 bye offering Burden an extra week to recover. Burden extended his touchdown streak to three games with a 56-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter.

Taylor recorded one catch for 11 yards on two targets in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Even with Garrett Wilson (concussion) inactive, Taylor's two targets were his fewest in a game since Week 2, and he left that one early with a thumb injury. It was Kenyon Sadiq who had Geno Smith's eyes against Kansas City, as the rookie tight end recorded four grabs for 49 yards on four targets. Taylor is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option at the position.

Rams head coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday during his appearance on the "Coach McVay Show" that he remains hopeful Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) will return from injured reserve this season, though he was unwilling to guarantee that the tight end will be activated by the time his 21-day evaluation window closes, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. "I'm reluctant to get too far ahead of anything, just because -- but yes, that is something we'd want to avoid if he's not prepared," McVay said, regarding the possibility of Ferguson being shut down. After missing five consecutive games while recovering from an ankle sprain, Ferguson appeared poised to return from IR ahead of this past Sunday's game against the Commanders, but his activation was delayed after he pulled his hamstring while running a route during Friday's practice. McVay said after the practice that the setback would likely keep Ferguson out for "a couple more weeks." Ferguson's 21-day window will come to a close Nov. 25, so even if he doesn't resume practicing before then, he'll likely need to show the Rams that he's made at least some progress in his recovery from the hamstring injury to get activated. McVay said that he would be open to adding Ferguson back to the 53-man roster before he's ready to play, but the Rams may not be keen on essentially playing a man down for more than a game or two.

Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

The Chiefs designated Norman-Lott (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday. Norman-Lott was limited in his return to practice Wednesday. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.

Judkins carried the ball 15 times for 43 yards and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. The Browns' running game once again struggled, with the team averaging just 2.8 yards per carry overall, and Judkins' longest gain went for only 12 yards. Dylan Sampson saw a season-high 11 touches to Judkins' 16, and the backfield could be drifting toward a timeshare as coach Todd Monken looks for solutions. Judkins has topped 70 rushing yards in a game just once all season, and he seems unlikely to break out in a Week 10 meeting with the Texans.

Meyers caught two passes for 47 yards on three targets in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. With Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on injured reserve, Meyers has settled in as the Bengals' third receiver behind target hogs Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Meyers would need an injury to one of those two to become relevant again in fantasy.

Downs (concussion) has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Downs upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice, clearing the league's concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts. The rookie first-rounder is all set to suit up for the contest as the starting slot cornerback and reserve punt returner for the Cowboys.

Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville. Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

The Cowboys designated Moore (hip) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. The fourth-round rookie cornerback has yet to play in a game this regular season after being placed on injured reserve ahead of the Week 1 opener. Once he does return to action, Moore will provide depth behind Joey Porter (ankle), DaRon Bland, Caleb Downs and Cobie Durant.

Washington turned six carries into minus-three yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. The rookie running back wasn't targeted in the passing game. One week after getting a trial run as the Raiders' clear lead back, a game in which he produced 83 yards on 25 carries, Washington was out-snapped 32 to 17 by Ashton Jeanty against San Francisco. He's averaging just 3.9 yards per carry on 71 totes this season and has just three receptions, though it's worth noting that Jeanty has been even less efficient as a ball carrier with only 3.1 YPC. Washington is a fantasy bench stash, but the Raiders' rushing attack seems broken as a whole.

Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore. Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

Titans head coach Robert Saleh said Monday that Singleton is "getting better," and the rookie running back could be a candidate to see added opportunities in the second half of the season if lead back Tony Pollard is dealt ahead of Tuesday's deadline, Turron Davenport of ESPN.com reports. A fifth-round pick out of Penn State, Singleton was a healthy inactive for four of the Titans' first eight games prior to a Week 9 bye and has logged more snaps on special teams than offense thus far during his rookie season. However, with the 29-year-old Pollard set to become a free agent after the season and likely not part of the 1-7 Titans' rebuilding effort, playing time could become up for grabs in the backfield if Tennessee receives an appealing trade offer for the veteran. Along with Singleton, Tyjae Spears (knee) and Michael Carter would be vying for reps in the event Pollard is traded, while Julius Chestnut is another option in the backfield but has been utilized almost exclusively on special teams.

Cuevas didn't garner a target in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars. Cuevas split time with nine snaps on both offense and special teams. This game marked the fourth time this season that the rookie had zero targets. Prior to Thursday night, the 23-year-old saw multiple targets in four straight games. He will likely have a similar role as the season continues.

Randall (neck) is officially listed as questionable for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports. Randall was not considered to be limited during Baltimore's walkthrough practice Wednesday but he's still on IR going into game-day. If he's not activated for Week 9, his next opportunity to make his regular-season debut would come in Week 10 versus the Chargers.

Allen failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets. Allen made the start at wide receiver but ran just 13 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 36 dropbacks against New York. With Xavier Worthy (hamstring) now injured, Allen could have a path to more playing time moving forward, but all three of Rashee Rice, Kenneth Walker and Travis Kelce are well ahead of the rookie wideout for targets.

Smack (calf) was limited in Wednesday's practice. It's a new injury for the Packers' rookie kicker, who went a perfect 7-for-7 on kicks in last Sunday's demolition of the Patriots. The team doesn't currently employ another kicker on the active roster or practice squad.

Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while adding three rushes for 13 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. Fagnano drew the start with both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) on injured reserve, and the undrafted rookie signal-caller unsurprisingly had a difficult night after also struggling in emergency duty against the Bills just four days earlier. Fagnano had been dealing with an ankle injury stemming from his aforementioned NFL debut and had little practice time on a short week, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle kept the game plan simple and focused on the short areas of the field, resulting in Fagnano averaging just 3.3 yards per attempt. Both of Fagnano's second-half picks also led to Jacksonville field goals, making it a forgettable night overall. With the Ravens reportedly putting the finishing touches on a trade with the Cardinals for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, Fagnano is likely to move into a reserve role as soon as a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

Johnson rushed six times for 34 yards and a touchdown and returned one kickoff for 29 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. The Chiefs held a 28-12 lead by the end of three quarters, which provided the opportunity for head coach Andy Reid to give Kenneth Walker, who scored three total touchdowns, some down time in the latter portion of the contest. Johnson took advantage of his opportunities, recording a six-yard touchdown run with 3:35 remaining. The rookie fifth-round pick's yardage total was a new career high, while his carry tally was his highest since Week 3. Johnson will remain in a modest No. 2 role for a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

Bailey (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. After missing Week 8 with the groin injury he suffered the previous week, Bailey appears poised to return after missing just one contest. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Bailey has piled up 35 tackles (21 solo), including 5.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.

Saints coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that Tyson should get "a healthy dose more" of snaps in Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports. Tyson played just 18 snaps and lost a fumble on his first catch this past Sunday against the Browns, but there were some positives from his regular-season debut, including a strong target rate (five targets on 16 routes). While there's no assurance of a full-time role, Tyson at least figures to take more snaps away from fellow rookie Bryce Lance, if not from veteran Devaughn Vele.

Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

Boston isn't slated to practice Wednesday due to a toe injury, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports. Boston logged a 93 percent offensive snap share in this past Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints en route to hauling in six of his seven targets for 98 yards. However the rookie WR emerged from the contest with a toe issue that will make his status worth watching ahead of this weekend's game against the Texans. If Boston -- who's expected to return to practice Thursday, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer -- ends up being available, he'll be catching passes once again from Deshaun Watson, while Week 9 starter Shedeur Sanders will revert to serving as the Browns' QB2.

Williams caught three passes for 25 yards on six targets in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. With Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the year, Williams led the team's wide receivers and tight ends in snaps and routes against Los Angeles, but it was a tough matchup against a top-tier pass defense. Williams should have better games moving forward in one of the league's pass-happiest offenses. The rookie wideout should be a full-time player down the stretch in the second half of the season.

Fields caught three of five targets for 40 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The rookie wideout is a distant third in the pecking order for targets behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely in the New York offense. For the season, Fields has 19 catches for 288 yards and one touchdown on 35 targets, averaging 36.0 yards per game across eight contests.
